subject: Boundary reshuffle and growth lanes: renewal coordination for Dataspark
messages:
From: Luis Rojas <luis@dataspark.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@dataspark.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal term + capacity reshuffle — request for options

Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with Maya, our usage profile jumped more than we projected in Q3 and our current renewal is coming up Jan 15. We need two things resolved before legal pushes the PO: 1) align the contract boundary to our fiscal year (Apr–Mar) without a hard penalty for mid-year top-ups, and 2) a clear, staged onramp so we can increase dedicated capacity across H1.

I attached a small export of Q3 usage for reference. Can you share a couple of structure options (multi-year with staged capacity, or an annualized commit with quarterly true-ups) and any pricing implications? Also — procurement wants to understand whether auto-renew would apply if we move to an annualized model.

Best,
Luis

Attachment: Dataspark_Q3_usage_summary.csv (csv, 72KB)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Luis Rojas <luis@dataspark.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@dataspark.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal term + capacity reshuffle — request for options

Luis — thanks for the usage export, that helps. High level: we can present two viable tracks that meet procurement needs and keep unit economics predictable.

Option A — Multi‑year ramped commit (3x year lanes):
- 36‑month term; annual committed token buckets that step up each year (you get a price break for the multi‑yr commitment).
- Quarterly canary onramp windows to allow +10–15% burst capacity without penalty (one per quarter).
- True‑up at each annual anniversary with rollover credits for any shortfall up to 8% to avoid mid‑term disputes.

Option B — Annualized commit with cadence top‑ups (preferred for fiscal alignment):
- 12‑month term aligned to your Apr–Mar fiscal year.
- Quarterly true‑ups and a staggered invoice cadence (Q1 invoice can be pro‑rated).
- Auto‑renew opt‑in is available; Procurement can opt out by giving 60 days notice prior to renewal.

If you want, we can mix elements: a 24‑month contract that annualizes billing to your FY but preserves some multi‑yr pricing benefit. I’ll draft a short amendment that shows the numbers for the two paths. Looping in Jordan for pricing confirmation.

Next steps: Jordan to provide a pro‑forma with price ladders and Ben to sign off on any non‑standard concessions.

—Chloe

Attachment: proposed_boundary_reshuffle_v2.pdf (pdf, 110KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Luis Rojas <luis@dataspark.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@dataspark.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal term + capacity reshuffle — request for options

Chloe/Luis — ran the numbers on both tracks; roughs below (rounded):

Option A (36m ramp):
- Year 1 commit: 2.5B tokens; Year 2: 4.0B; Year 3: 6.0B
- Effective blended unit: $0.00035/token with multi‑yr rebate at signed commit
- Annual true‑up cap: 8% rollover credit

Option B (12m fiscal align):
- Annual commit aligned Apr–Mar: 4.5B tokens
- Quarterly true‑ups with pro‑rata invoicing; unit: $0.00041/token
- Auto‑renew: available; default is off unless Procurement selects opt‑in box (we will honor written notice).

Concessions we can consider for Dataspark: one accelerated onboarding credit to cover migration costs, and a 60‑day SLO credit window tied to latency targets for production traffic.

Ben — any objections to the rebate language (multiyear) or the SLO credit?

Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Luis Rojas <luis@dataspark.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal term + capacity reshuffle — request for options

All — fine with the structure. Two guardrails from revenue side:
1) Any multi‑year rebate is contingent on full payment schedule (we can do annual invoicing but need commitment language around non‑cancellation in the first 12 months without repayment of rebates).
2) Keep the annual true‑up cap as described (8%) and allow a one‑time re‑calibration if usage delta exceeds 40% vs forecast in any quarter (we’ll negotiate true‑up mechanics in amendment).

Chloe — please prepare a clean amendment that shows the two options side‑by‑side with explicit invoice cadence and a single paragraph on auto‑renew mechanics for Procurement to review. Luis/Maya — happy to hop on a 30‑minute call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Ben

Signature:
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Luis Rojas <luis@dataspark.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@dataspark.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@dataspark.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal term + capacity reshuffle — request for options

Appreciate the fast turnaround — this gives Procurement the language they need. Two quick asks before the amendment: 1) can you put the auto‑renew clause in plain language (we need the exact notice window and whether auto‑renew defaults on or off), and 2) can you include an annex that shows how quarterly canary bursts will be billed (e.g., how many bursts allowed per year and the overage rate)?

If you can get the amendment + annex over by Friday EOD our legal team will expedite the PO. If a short call helps, Maya and I can do Thu 4–4:30 PT.

Thanks — Luis
